claim: Names the in-world source the light is pretending to come from, which decides colour temperature, shadow direction and hardness in one word. A director sets this first: sun and neon give you two completely different films of the same scene, and 'unmotivated' is the honest label for the flat generator default nobody chose.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: overcast ambient light, diffused skylight, shadowless
lit by a visible lamp in frame, warm point light source, glowing fixture
firelight, orange flame glow, warm flickering light
screen light, pale blue glow on face, monitor lit
neon lights, neon glow, magenta and cyan light spill
fluorescent lighting, cold white overhead tubes, faint green cast
streetlamp glow, sodium orange pool of light from above
car headlights, harsh white beam from the front, headlight glare
magical glow, unnatural glowing light source, arcane light
bioluminescent glow, soft teal organic light, glowing in the dark
flat even lighting, no visible light source, sourceless illumination
mixed lighting, two light sources, warm and cool light clashing

review.issue: sky_ambient ("overcast ambient light, diffused skylight, shadowless") and unmotivated ("flat even lighting, no visible light source, sourceless illumination") describe the same frame — flat, shadowless, no directional cue — and will render as the same panel. Both also collide with light.quality.overcast_flat, light.ratio.flat_1_1 and light.key_dir.ambient_none, so four cards would ship the same image.
review.fix: Give sky_ambient the thing that actually distinguishes open shade — colour and sky direction: "overcast sky, cool blue-grey daylight, soft shadowless light from above". Make unmotivated the empty-clause baseline panel, since that is literally what it is: the generator default nobody chose. Then delete ambient_none from light.key_dir (see separate note) and let light.quality own overcast_flat.
